significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a "low-dimensional, causally manipulable subspace" provides monotonic control of trace length and yields an accuracy-length response with a shortening plateau followed by a truncation cliff; this is form (iii), a functional relation with a threshold, rather than merely an encoding claim. It establishes both a mechanism for verbosity and a behavioral phenomenon that would constrain how inference-compute policies allocate tokens, a consequential issue in test-time-compute work such as Snell et al. (2024) and Muennighoff et al.'s s1 (2025). Verified false, it would rule out the simple low-dimensional control account or the claimed accuracy-preserving regime, although the bundled assertions make that branch less discriminating; true and false nevertheless identify distinguishable states. After topic substitution, efficient reasoning alone would not imply this particular monotonic plateau-and-cliff law, so the above-median score derives from the claim rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is explicitly a "training-free, interpretable dial for compute allocation," implemented as the "length-steering vector"; it is ex ante because its coefficient is selected during inference before the final answer and token cost are realized. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts smooth, monotonic length changes and an accuracy-preserving interval, so more than a search procedure survives recalibration, though neither cross-model transfer nor a universal threshold is asserted. The likely downstream users include researchers and practitioners controlling inference cost, but the hypothesis does not firmly claim scope across architectures or training regimes—the cross-task statement is framed as something to test—limiting broad deployment reach. Under topic substitution, generic efficient reasoning supplies neither this inference-time knob nor its lead time, so the reach credit is claim-specific.
